## Beaked Whale Detection and Classification

Beaked whale echolocation clicks were detected and classified using methods developed for previous DASBR surveys in the California Current (Keating et al. 2018; Simonis et al. 2020; Rankin et al. 2024).

- Acoustic recordings were decimated to 288 kHz and processed using the Click Detector module in [PAMGuard](https://www.pamguard.org/) (v. 2.02.14).

- Recordings were high-pass filtered at 10 kHz, with an additional 80 kHz whitening filter applied to flatten the ambient noise spectrum.

- Click detection was performed on the upper hydrophone (HTI-92-WB) using a 12 dB signal-to-noise ratio threshold. PAMGuard settings for each deployment are available [here](https://github.com/SAEL-SWFSC/CalCurCEAS-2024-Drifter-Analysis/tree/main/_data/BeakedWhales/PamgaurdSettings).

- An experienced analyst (AES) manually reviewed detections in PAMGuard Viewer Mode and identified beaked whale acoustic events based on click frequency, waveform and spectral characteristics, inter-click interval, and angle of arrival.

- Acoustic events were defined as three or more echolocation clicks from a given species within 2 or more minutes.

- Events were classified to species or signal type using established characteristics of beaked whale echolocation signals (see \[Beaked Whale ID Guide\](BeakedWhales-IDGuide.qmd)). Species acoustically identified in this study included goose-beaked (*Ziphius cavirostris*), Baird's (*Berardius bairdii*), Stejneger's (*Mesoplodon stejnegeri*), Hubbs' (*Mesoplodon carlhubbsi*), and ginkgo-toothed (*Mesoplodon ginkgodens*) beaked whales, along with unidentified and possible beaked whale categories.

- All events were classified twice by the same analyst for quality control.

## Ziphius Abundance Estimation

Density and abundance of goose-beaked whales (*Ziphius cavirostris*) were estimated using the group-based acoustic point-transect approach developed by Barlow et al. (2021).

- Acoustic effort was divided into two-minute snapshots and each snapshot was classified according to the presence or absence of goose-beaked whale echolocation clicks.

- Effective detection area was estimated from the distribution of vertical arrival angles using the maximum simulated likelihood approach of Barlow et al. (2021).

- Acoustic availability was estimated from observed encounter durations using the mark-recapture approach of Barlow et al. (2021).

- Group density was estimated from the proportion of snapshots containing detections, corrected for effective survey area and acoustic availability.

- Group density was converted to animal density using a mean group size of 1.9, and abundance was estimated by extrapolating density across the study area.

- Uncertainty in the components of the abundance estimate was incorporated using a Bayesian estimation procedure.

Code associated with the abundance analysis is available in the [Beaked Whale Abundance Estimation repository](https://github.com/asimonis/Beaked-Whale-Abundance-Estimation).
